newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark to continue fiscal tightening through 1998.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to continue fiscal tightening through 1998.

text.p: Danish Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft said on Tuesday that he would continue fiscal tightening in 1998 but did not say if it would be at the 1996 and 1997 levels of 0.5 percent.

"We have been tightening the fiscal policy every year since 1994, and we'll do that also this year. And the budget we've prepared for '98 will also build in a tightening," Lykketoft said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"I can't tell you exactly how much, but it will be such a fiscal policy which is necessary in a situation where the economy is booming," he added.
He echoed Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen's pledge of continuity, despite the resignation from the minority coalition government just before Christmas of the Centre Democrat party.

The party, which held the trade and health portfolios, said it was alarmed by the government's increasing dependence on the far left and could no longer remain in the cabinet but that its five members of parliament would continue to back the coalition.
"I don't think it's very likely that we will have an early election," Lykketoft said. "The parliamentary situation has not changed, basically, because the Centre Democrats left the government."

"They are still a part of the parliamentary majority supporting this government and even without the Centre Democrats we have a parliamentary majority backing the existence of this government," he said.

"We made a number of agreements with the left-wing parties which in no way whatsoever change the general line of the economic policy. The stability of Danish economic policy is totally untouched and the reaction of the markets has been to recognise that fact."
